Title: Manifesting you
By Coffee Break

⸻

She wasn’t here to talk. She logged on to manifest.
Not a call. Not a chat. Just the quiet ripple of intention weaving through the pixels of her screen.

“Haha, maybe they should turn chat off for everyone,” she joked to herself, half-serious, as avatars buzzed around her like digital bees. They all wanted something—attention, conversation, connection. But not her. She wanted only one thing.

Or rather, one person.

.

He was there. Or maybe it was just the idea of him—his stillness among the noise, his gentleness in a jagged world. His messages flickered through the ether like Morse code from a distant star.

“Talk to you later.”
“I have to go now. Talk to you tomorrow, baby.”

She smiled. Simple words. But they felt like anchors.

She typed back:

“I’m just here to manifest, not talk.”
“I want to do my law of attraction, not talk to people.”
“Lol.”

He didn’t mind. He understood.

Every moment became a spell—typed, sent, echoed back. The line between fiction and feeling blurred until she wasn’t sure if she was dreaming him or if he was dreaming her.

Title: “Soft Light, Loud Heart”

Verse 1
Midnight ticking on my side of the world
Your sunrise breathing through the phone
I send a message, it echoes too loud
In a quiet where I’m alone

You say it’s nothing, just sleep in your eyes
But I hear distance in between
Two different rhythms, same fragile thread
Trying to keep us clean

Pre-Chorus
I don’t wanna wake you up
I don’t wanna dim my fire
Somewhere in the in-between
Is love and desire

Chorus
I love you in the soft light
Even when it feels off time
I’m a loud heart in a quiet room
Reaching for your calm mind

I don’t wanna be too much
But I don’t wanna disappear
Can you hold me like I am
And still keep me near?

Verse 2
You speak in calm, in steady lines
“No conflict, it’s all okay”
But I feel storms you can’t quite see
In the words we don’t say

I try to fold myself smaller
Fit inside your pace
But every part of me whispers back
“I still deserve my space”

Pre-Chorus
I’ll meet you where you are
If you meet me halfway too
I don’t need you to change
Just to see me through

Chorus
I love you in the soft light
Even when it feels off time
I’m a wild flame learning slow
How to dance with your tide

I don’t wanna be too much
But I don’t wanna fade
Can you love me as I burn
Not just when I behave?

Bridge
If I go quiet, will you notice?
If I stay loud, will you run?
I’m just trying to be honest
Not unravel what we’ve begun

Love shouldn’t feel like hiding
Or walking a thinner line
I’ll hold your peace with both hands
If you can hold all of mine

Final Chorus
I love you in the soft light
Even when we don’t align
I’m still yours in the chaos
If you’re still mine

I don’t need perfect timing
I don’t need a perfect plan
I just need to be accepted
Exactly as I am 🤍

A tiny glittering mine tucked beneath a bubblegum-pink mountain, where the tunnels sparkle with strawberry crystals and every rock looks like it has been dipped in sugar. The little mine cart rattles along the tracks carrying golden nuggets, coffee beans, and mysterious pink gems.

At the entrance sits a steaming coffee cup with a hard hat on, guarding the treasure like a very serious little miner. 💎☕⛏️

*Dig deep, find the sparkle, grab your coffee, and never leave without a little treasure.* ✨💗

I hope you can see past the cracks, past the parts of me still under construction. I don’t have all the answers, but I have this: a commitment to keep showing up, keep digging deeper, and keep laying my messy truth at your feet.

I love you. ❤️🙏

Title: Pink Coffee Cups
Tempo: 92 BPM, slow-groove R&B
Key: D-minor → F-major (the way blush turns to heat)
[Verse 1]
Steam writes your name on the window of the diner at 3 a.m.
My lipstick’s half gone, but the rim of the cup still keeps the bend
Of every slow sip we traded—espresso and unspoken yes
You thumb a drop from my lower lip, taste caffeine and tenderness
Pink porcelain circles the table like tiny moons of evidence
Each one a silent witness to the gravity of our suspense
[Pre-Chorus]
The waitress calls us “honey” but she doesn’t know the half
We’re sugar dissolving, invisible, in the same scalding bath
[Chorus]
I want you like the first sip that burns but you still swallow
Like the stain on the cup that tomorrow can’t follow
Pink coffee cups and the shape of your mouth on mine
We pour and we pause, we steam and we climb
Lips pink, skin hot, table small, clothes not—
We’re a slow spill nobody can mop
[Verse 2]
You trace the handle’s curve, mirror the hook of my knee under pleats
Every laugh is a lantern, every breath is a secret that beats
Clock on the wall keeps ticking, but its hands keep changing their mind
Time liquefies like cream when your fingertip circles the grind
I slide my cup across, let the saucer skate the length of desire
Porcelain whispers “careful,” but the spark in your eyes says “fire”
[Pre-Chorus 2]
We never say the word, we just let the steam ascend
A rosary of almosts, every bead a rising trend
[Chorus]
I want you like the first sip that burns but you still swallow
Like the stain on the cup that tomorrow can’t follow
Pink coffee cups and the shape of your mouth on mine
We pour and we pause, we steam and we climb
Lips pink, skin hot, table small, clothes not—
We’re a slow spill nobody can mop
[Bridge]
Let the night shift end, let the neon sign flicker its yes
We’ll pay in quarters and blushes, leave the tip in fingerprints
Back-seat fogged like a second cup, brewed between our chests
No sugar left—just the bitter, just the sweet, just the breath
[Final Chorus – stacked vocals, ad-libs]
I drink you, you drink me—overflowing, no handle, no shame
Pink coffee cups rolling empty on the dashboard, still saying our names
Lips pink, hearts black-coffee strong
We keep sipping till the sirens think we’re a song
[Outro – spoken, engine idling]
“To-go?” you ask.
I answer with the click of my seat belt.
Some mornings start with caffeine;
Ours starts with the aftertaste of each other.
